description: Canonical terms for the Ontology Extraction Framework wiki.

aliases: 本体驱动信息抽取框架
keywords.short: A framework that uses ontology definitions to govern source-grounded information extraction from unstructured data.
keywords.definition: An Ontology Extraction Framework defines concept types, canonical domain concepts, extraction schemas, validation rules, evidence objects and review workflows so unstructured text can be converted into auditable structured knowledge.

keywords.short: A source-grounded structured extraction library used as the execution layer.
keywords.definition: LangExtract is positioned here as the extraction execution layer: it uses extraction classes, attributes, prompt rules and examples to extract structured instances from source text while preserving grounding spans.

keywords.short: The layer that defines how ontology concepts themselves are defined and governed.
keywords.definition: A meta-ontology specifies concept type definitions, fields, required attributes, validation rules, extraction classes, examples, review policies, status and versioning. It manages the structure of domain ontologies rather than individual report facts.

keywords.short: The domain-specific concept system for LCA, GHG, Scope 3, units, standards and boundaries.
keywords.definition: A domain ontology defines canonical concepts, aliases, hierarchy, standard references, expected fields, allowed units, extraction hints and audit notes for a professional domain such as LCA or GHG accounting.

keywords.short: The task-specific subset of ontology used to generate extraction prompts and validation schemas.
keywords.definition: An extraction ontology selects concept types, canonical concept filters, fields, source-grounding rules, missing-evidence behavior, LangExtract settings and post-validation steps for a specific extraction run.

keywords.short: A schema definition for a family of extractable entities.
keywords.definition: A concept type defines what fields, constraints, validation rules and review policies apply to a family of entities, such as GHG emission metrics, LCA claims or missing disclosures.

keywords.short: A stable standard concept in the domain ontology.
keywords.definition: A canonical concept is a normalized domain concept such as ghg.scope2.market_based or ghg.scope3.category1, with definition, aliases, parent concept, standard references and expected fields.

keywords.short: The declared type, requirement and constraint for a field in a concept type.
keywords.definition: A field definition states the name, type, requiredness, allowed values, dependency rules and description for one attribute in an extractable concept type.

keywords.short: The atomic output of ontology-guided extraction.
keywords.definition: An Evidence Object is an extracted entity bound to a concept type, canonical concept, source quote, page, fields, applicability label, missing fields, audit flags, confidence, review status and ontology version.

keywords.short: Binding an extraction to the exact source text or page that supports it.
keywords.definition: Source grounding records the original quote, page, section, file and optionally character interval that support an extracted entity, making unsupported outputs visible and reviewable.

keywords.short: A required or expected disclosure that is absent or insufficient in the source document.
keywords.definition: Missing evidence is treated as a first-class output when a report lacks expected support for a concept, field, method, unit, boundary or baseline. The system records the gap rather than inventing a value.

keywords.short: A domain expert rule made explicit in ontology, validation or review logic.
keywords.definition: An expert heuristic is a professional judgment such as 'materiality statements are not quantified inventory' or 'product LCA readiness requires a functional unit', represented as ontology constraints, validation rules, applicability rules or audit flags.

keywords.short: A machine-checkable rule that tests extracted fields or concept mappings.
keywords.definition: A validation rule checks constraints such as required fields, unit compatibility, Scope 3 category presence, source quote availability and separation of location-based versus market-based emissions.

keywords.short: A rule that determines what task an extracted evidence object can safely support.
keywords.definition: An applicability rule maps evidence quality and completeness to labels such as product_lca_ready, screening_lca_ready, corporate_inventory_ready, scope3_evidence_ready, weak_signal_only or review_required.

keywords.short: The rate at which weak or insufficient evidence is incorrectly marked as ready for a stronger task.
keywords.definition: False-ready rate measures dangerous overclaiming, such as marking weak narrative disclosure as product_lca_ready when expert review says it lacks functional unit, boundary, method or inventory detail.

keywords.short: An append-only record of expert decisions and corrections on extracted evidence.
keywords.definition: A review ledger records reviewer, evidence ID, decision, corrections, notes and timestamp so ontology extraction quality can be audited and errors can feed back into ontology refinement.

keywords.short: Recording which ontology version produced or validated each extraction.
keywords.definition: Ontology versioning makes concept definitions, field schemas, validation rules and extracted evidence reproducible by recording version IDs in concept definitions, extraction runs and evidence objects.

keywords.short: A record of ontology edits and their rationale.
keywords.definition: An ontology change log records what changed, which objects were affected, why the change was made, and which version came before and after the change.

keywords.short: An agent whose behavior is constrained by domain ontology, validation, evidence and review workflows.
keywords.definition: A professional agent is not merely a general LLM with a domain prompt; it operationalizes expert heuristics through ontology, schemas, validation rules, source grounding, missing-evidence detection and human review loops.

keywords.short: A graph generated on demand from retrieved evidence objects rather than pre-materializing all possible edges.
keywords.definition: A Lazy Knowledge Graph stores evidence objects, metadata, embeddings and provenance first, then dynamically creates local graph nodes and edges for a query, comparison or visualization task.
